fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Lord of the Rings as Guiding Myth", "body": "David Whitehead explains why he launched a four-part Truth Warrior series with Laura Lee on The Lord of the Rings as the guiding myth of our time. Reading from her synopsis, he says the tale matters not because it is new but because it draws on a body of ancient knowledge obscured through distortion and deception, and he describes rewatching the trilogy during lockdown to find strength. In his view Tolkien gathered myths and legends from many traditions, with echoes of the Bhagavad Gita, into a story rooted in the Western magical tradition. Chance adds that he has read, heard and watched the saga repeatedly over the past year."}, {"title": "The Archetypes Live Inside Us", "body": "Drawing on Carl Jung, David lists the persona, shadow, anima or animus and self alongside the wise old man, the hero and the trickster, and suggests that the Fellowship, Sauron and Saruman are all figures within each reader, echoing Joseph Campbell's line that the heavens and hells live inside us. Chance describes meeting Gandalf as a spirit guide during a meditative exercise, and offers his view that ignored archetypes return in tyrannical outer form to tear down the ego. David argues that a priest class literalized myth, and reads the saying that the kingdom of heaven is within you as a call to inner relationship rather than worship."}, {"title": "Evil, Fear and the Ring of Power", "body": "Chance recalls David's line from the Laura Lee series that a moral victory requires choice, choice requires freedom, and freedom is exactly what the Ring of Power takes away. David points to Boromir, who wants to wield the Ring for good, as a picture of well-meaning people persuaded that the ends justify the means, and to Frodo's innocence as the quality that lets him bear it. He argues that evil must be admitted to exist, that meaning well is not enough, and that lingering fear and evil are closely tied. His remedy is to study fear and integrate the shadow through art, martial arts or calligraphy rather than repress it."}, {"title": "Creativity and the Next Step", "body": "Chance shares a pet theory that creative people are decisive: faced with a blank canvas or page, the artist takes the first step and trusts the next one to become clear. He links the artist's flow state to the synchronicity of the hero's journey, where the Fellowship never sees the whole road but takes the next step through Caradhras, Moria and Lothlorien, and he suggests that facing today's troubles is likewise one step at a time on the way to Mount Doom. David calls this a source of hope, recalling how often the story hangs on a thread, and says a voice of doubt accompanies every creative step."}, {"title": "Freedom Versus Liberty in David's View", "body": "David sums up what he believes is worth preserving in Western civilization as freedom, which he separates from liberty. Liberty, he says, is something a government grants, while freedom is the ground of your being and rests on individual sovereignty, free but not free to take another's freedom. He credits individual genius, quoting Walter Russell, with the West's achievements, and contrasts the histories of China and the West, arguing that communism turned Chinese civilization from its course, though he voices deep respect for its martial arts. Chance suggests communism may act like an egregore in the collective psyche, and that what people call God is, at root, freedom."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Sensei Dave returns to InnerVerse to help bring out the Truth Warrior in all of us. In this eclectic conversation, we examine the "defining myth of our time," JRR Tolkien's LOTR trilogy, and finding spiritual guidance for our strange times through the archetype of the hero. We also look at the One Ring and what it says about the nature of fear and evil, the link between the Hero's Journey and the creative flow state, and a lot more.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Myths as an archive of buried history", "body": "David Whitehead describes the Bock Saga, a Finnish and Swedish family tradition that Michael Tsarion explored on Unslaved, as another missing chapter in the story of the West. He argues that when libraries are burned and records locked away, myths and legends become the place where memory survives, and that ancient people encoded history in story rather than in the left brained, analytical style modern schooling trains. Whether the saga proves literal or folkloric, Chance Garton frames it as another telling of the defining myth of our times, the struggle between good and evil."}, {"title": "Rethinking hell and religious authority", "body": "Chance Garton recounts the Bock Saga's claim that hell was once the name of a real place, the seat of an older Western culture, before it was recast as a lake of fire to frighten believers. David Whitehead extends this through Ralph Ellis, a revisionist historian who reads the Bible and the Arthurian legend on exoteric and esoteric levels. David stresses that he is not asking Christians to drop their faith, and both men praise Christian allies, while arguing that fear of eternal damnation has been used to keep people obedient rather than free."}, {"title": "Communism and religion as parallel control systems", "body": "David Whitehead argues that communism makes the state into God, drawing on Ayn Rand's mystics of spirit and mystics of muscle and on Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn's Warnings to the West. In his view, the gulag of the communist state and the threat of hell in dogmatic religion work the same way, one punishing people in this life and the other in the next. Chance Garton adds that any external surveillance state must first be built inside the mind, which is why both men treat inner freedom and the courage to ask questions as the first line of defense."}, {"title": "Martial arts and the unity of mind and body", "body": "Picking up Chance Garton's mention of Wilhelm Reich and the home workouts David posts on Patreon, David Whitehead describes how martial arts carried him through dark times when other methods failed. He frames training as inner combat against laziness, self doubt and limiting beliefs, and compares a harmonized mind and body to a well tuned instrument. David reports students who say their lives improved after training, while calling himself only a guide. Chance adds that whole body movement trains the true will, the part of you that gets up when another part insists you are lazy."}, {"title": "Awakening the warrior and hero archetype", "body": "David Whitehead sees the warrior as an archetype in everyone, and warns that repressing it lets tyranny appear outside in the world instead. He points to farm tools turned into weapons by oppressed peoples, and to the double edged sword, one blade turned inward against your own demons and one outward against threats to freedom. Speaking during the 2020 lockdowns, David calls on listeners to warrior up, holding that a true warrior stays optimistic, and that seeking knowledge as a relationship rather than a possession brings unseen forces to your aid."}]

fields.Plus Quotes JSON: [{"text": "What people forget is that ancient man did not think the way modern man does. That is a green language way or right brain way of looking at the very notion of sovereignty.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "In order to bring about the external control system and the total surveillance state, technocratic ultimate version of communistic lockdown and destruction of freedom, it has to be done in the mind first before it could ever express in the external.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "We're not designed to be unheroic in our lives. fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "The way we're taught to view the world is that the world is something happening to us.
